gold_answer: Check that the linear actuator auxiliary box is electrically connected and its adjustments are verified before starting the motor. Also verify that the brushes are in good condition and can move freely in the brush holders.

8.4.2 Brush sparking
Any possible sparking of the brushes can be observed through a window in the slip ring enclosure. Sparking is often
an indication of inadequate operation. Measures to prevent sparking must be taken immediately. The reasons of
sparking shall be cleared up and undisturbed running restored. Possible causes for sparking:
• Inadequate loading condition
• Brushes sticking in their holders
• Brushes too loose in their holders
• Loose connection of brush terminal
• Imperfect brush bedding
• Incorrect or unequal brush pressure
• The sliding surfaces of the slip-rings are deteriorated
• The type of carbon brushes is not acceptable for the operating conditions
• Misalignment of shaft couplings
• The machine is out of balance
• Worn bearings giving unequal air gaps.

Before the motor is started for the first time, the following items must be thoroughly checked:
• The lifting mechanism must be in the start position, that is the short circuit ring in open position, and the

and clarified before continuing usage.
The short circuit ring shall be in open position, that is in the position where the contact females of the short circuit
ring do not make any contact with the male contact elements of the slip ring assembly.
The electric movement limits (R1-E1), must be checked and adjusted just before to reach the mechanical limit of the
liner actuator motor so that the lifting mechanism will stop at proper position.

7.7.4 Care of brush lifting device
The slip ring assembly and slip ring housing shall be checked at regular service intervals.
For brush lifting device, control the movement to be set and the contacts to be corrected every six months or 100

7.7.4.1 Brushes, brush holders
The brushes will normally wear in use and must be replaced before they are worn out. The brushes must be checked
at regular intervals and must be replaced latest when the wear has reached the wear limit mark. In case the limit mark
is not evident, the wear limit is about 10 mm from the brush top. When the brushes are replaced, the brush rocker
must be re-adjusted.
It must be checked also at regular intervals, that the brushes can freely move in the brush holders and that the brush
contact surfaces are in good condition, without burning marks.

question: What does the outlet-pressure monitoring function do on the Grundfos pump?
gold_answer: It monitors the pump outlet pressure. If pressure is below 5 bar for more than 5 seconds, a warning is given; if outlet pressure is above 7 bar for more than 8 seconds, the warning must be reset.

It can be configured with detection and resetting delays to manage alerts, such as issuing a warning if pressure falls below a lower limit for a set duration and clearing it once it rises above a higher limit [chunk:1]. Users can also adjust hysteresis bands and specify whether the function activates when pressure exceeds or drops below the target value [chunk:4]. Based on the available documentation, these settings provide flexible threshold management, though specific factory defaults or additional automated pump responses for this exact function are not fully detailed [chunk:1, chunk:4].

question: What does Alarm 5.9720, 6.9720, or 7.9720 relate to on a Haas rotary unit?
gold_answer: It relates to an encoder fault where software reports an internal encoder fault.

generation.generated_answer: Alarms 5.9720, 6.9720, and 7.9720 indicate an A, B, or C Axis Secondary Encoder Serial Fault [chunk:2]. These alarms correspond to specific subcodes, including an Encoder CRC Fault (subcode 0x4) and an Encoder Cable Fault (subcode 0x5) [chunk:3]. Common triggers involve linear scale signals disrupted by electrical noise from high-power cables or incorrectly connected cabling [chunk:2]. Resolving the issue requires inspecting the cables and connectors, and if the alarm remains, the rotary unit must be serviced [chunk:4].

question: Which PowerFlex 520 parameters should be set when Start and Speed Reference are controlled over RS-485 DSI?
gold_answer: Set P046 [Start Source 1] to 3 "Serial/DSI" if Start is controlled from the network. Set P047 [Speed Reference1] to 3 "Serial/DSI" if Speed Reference is controlled from the network. C123 [RS485 Data Rate] sets the RS-485 data rate, and all nodes must use the same data rate.

generation.generated_answer: To control Start and Speed Reference over an RS-485 DSI network, set P046 [Start Source 1] to 3 “Serial/DSI” and P047 [Speed Reference1] to 3 “Serial/DSI” [chunk:1]. You must also configure C123 [RS485 Data Rate] to match the setting on all other network nodes, and assign a unique value to C124 [RS485 Node Addr] for the drive [chunk:1]. These parameter adjustments direct the drive to accept both start commands and speed references directly from the DSI communication port [chunk:1].

The PowerFlex 525 Safe Torque Off function:
• Provides the Safe Torque Off function that is defined in EN 61800-5-2.

requirements of a system “Safe Torq ue Off” function that satisfies

EN 62061, IEC 61508, and EN 61800-5-2.

may not be as accurate as the Rotate Tune test.

This test is used when the motor is not coupled to the load or the load is low

Align the PM Angle
To align the PM angle, do the following:
1. Uncouple the load.
2. Set these parameters to the recommended value:
•A 5 1 7 [ P M D C I n j e c t C u r ] = 60% (default is 30%)
• A518 [PM Align Time] = 5.8 s (default is 0.7 s)
• A580 [Current Loop BW] = 300 Hz (default is 0 Hz)
3. Set the desired speed (10...40 Hz recommended).
Check the setting for P047 [Speed Reference 1]. Speed reference can be
from POT, control panel of Connected Components Workbench
software, and so on.
4. Set the Start Source.
Check the setting for P046 [Start Source 1]. Start source can be from POT,
control panel of Connected Components Workbench software, and so
on.
5. Start the drive to run at the desired speed.
6. Drive will begin to align itself (move forward and reverse) and run to the
desired speed.
7. Stop the drive. The drive is now aligned.

Adjustments if PM Angle Alignment has Failed
If the PM angle alignment has failed, do the following:
1. Cycle drive power or set A535 [Motor Fdbk Type] = 0 “None”, then set back
to 4 “Quadrature” or 5 “Quad Check”.
2. Increase A517 [PM DC Inject Cur] by 50%.
3. Increase A518 [PM Align Time] by 0.2 s.
4. Repeat the Align the PM Angle
instructions again, beginning from step 3.
The PM angle alignment only needs to be performed once unless the
drive is power cycled or re-tuned.
IMPORTANT The PM angle alignment has failed when fault F012 (HW Overcurrent) or
F013 (Ground Fault) is observed during acceleration and deceleration.

question: How do you acknowledge a motion control error with MC_Reset on an S7-1200 PLC?
gold_answer: Check the indicated requirements, start error acknowledgement with a rising edge at the Execute input parameter, and confirm acknowledgement when Done equals TRUE and <Axis name>.StatusBits.Error equals FALSE.

generation.generated_answer: To acknowledge a motion control error with MC_Reset, first eliminate the root cause of any pending configuration errors [chunk:3]. Next, trigger the acknowledgement by sending a rising edge (positive pulse) to the `Execute` input parameter [chunk:2]. The error is confirmed as cleared when the `Done` output becomes TRUE and the `<Axis name>.StatusBits.Error` status bit returns to FALSE [chunk:2]. Ensure the `Restart` parameter is set to FALSE, as this specific setting is used to acknowledge pending errors [chunk:4].
generation.clean_answer: To acknowledge a motion control error with MC_Reset, first eliminate the root cause of any pending configuration errors. Next, trigger the acknowledgement by sending a rising edge (positive pulse) to the `Execute` input parameter. The error is confirmed as cleared when the `Done` output becomes TRUE and the `<Axis name>.StatusBits.Error` status bit returns to FALSE. Ensure the `Restart` parameter is set to FALSE, as this specific setting is used to acknowledge pending errors.

gold_reference_evidence.quote:
To acknowledge an error with MC_Reset, follow these steps:
1. Check the requirements indicated above.
2. Start the acknowledgement of the error with a rising edge at the Execute input parameter.
3. The error has been acknowledged when Done equals TRUE and the technology object
tag <Axis name>.StatusBits.Error equals FALSE.

To disable an axis, follow these steps:
1. Bring the axis to a standstill.
You can identify when the axis is at a standstill in technology object tag <Axis
name>.StatusBits.StandStill.
2. Set input parameter "Enable" to FALSE after standstill is reached.
3. If output parameters "Busy" and "Status" and technology object tag <Axis
name>.StatusBits.Enable indicate the value FALSE, disabling of the axis is complete.

question: What does the Direction input specify for S7-1200 motion control?
gold_answer: The Direction input specifies the direction of rotation. Value 0 means the direction corresponds to the sign of the Velocity parameter by default, and value 1 indicates positive direction of rotation.

9.3.4 Operation of motion c ontrol for S7-1200
9.3.4.1 CPU outputs used for motion control
The CPU provides four pulse output generators. Each pulse output generator provides one
pulse output and one direction output for controlling a stepper motor drive or a servo motor
drive with pulse interface. The pulse output provides the drive with the pulses required for
motor motion. The direction output controls the travel direction of the drive.

question: How are completed and aborted S7-1200 motion control commands indicated?
gold_answer: A completed motion control task is indicated by TRUE in the output parameter Done. If the task is aborted during execution, it is indicated by TRUE in output parameter CommandAborted.

These boolean output parameters collectively signal whether a task is actively processing, has successfully concluded, or was interrupted by another motion control task [chunk:4].

9.3.6.1 Monitoring MC instructions with a "Done" output parameter
Motion control instructions with the output parameter "Done" are started by the input
parameter "Execute" and have a defined conclusion (for example, with motion control
instruction "MC_Home": Homing was successful). The task is complete and the axis is at a
standstill.
● The output parameter "Done" indicates the value TRUE, if the task has been successfully
completed.
● The output parameters "Busy", "CommandAborted", and "Error" signal that the task is still
being processed, has been aborted or an error is pending. The motion control instruction
"MC_Reset" cannot be aborted and thus has no "CommandAborted" output parameter.

7.5.1.2 Bearing temperature
The bearing temperatures are measured by Pt-100 resistance temperature detectors. Since a temperature rise
above the alarm limit can be caused either by increased losses in the bearing, or by decreased cooling capacity, it
often indicates a problem somewhere in the machine or in the lubrication system, and should therefore be closely
monitored.
The reasons for abnormal bearing temperature vary, but for some possible reason see Chapter 7.5.2 Lubrication of
sleeve bearings or Chapter 8.1.2 Lubrication system and bearings. If the temperature rise is followed by an increase
in vibration levels, the problem might also be related to the machine's alignment, see Chapter 3. Installation and
alignment or to damage in the bearing shells in which case the bearing needs to be dismantled and checked.

Using a drive with filter may result in relatively high ground leakage currents.
Therefore, the filter must only be used in installations with grounded AC
supply systems and be permanently installed and solidly grounded (bonded)
to the building power distribution ground. Ensure that the incoming supply
neutral is solidly connected (bonded) to the same building power distribution
ground. Grounding must not rely on flexible cables and should not include any
form of plug or socket that would permit inadvertent disconnection. Some
local codes may require redundant ground connections. The integrity of all
connections should be periodically checked.

question: If a PowerFlex drive shows an auxiliary-input fault and the S7-1200 motion logic is jogging an axis, what should be checked across the drive and PLC?
gold_answer: For the PowerFlex drive, F002 Auxiliary Input indicates an external trip input and the evidence says to check remote wiring and communications. For the S7-1200 motion logic, the JogForward/JogBackward parameters command axis movement and the Velocity parameter defines jog speed. The combined check is drive-side external-trip wiring/communications plus PLC-side jog command and velocity parameters.

requirements of a system “Safe Torq ue Off” function that satisfies

EN 62061, IEC 61508, and EN 61800-5-2.

9.1 High-speed counter
S7-1200 Programmable controller
You configure the parameters for each HSC in the device configuration for the CPU:
counting mode, I/O connections, interrupt assignment, and operation as a high-speed
counter or as a device to measure pulse frequency.
Some of the parameters for the HSC can be modified by your user program to provide
program control of the counting process:
● Set the counting direction to a NEW_DIR value
● Set the current count value to a NEW_CV value
● Set the reference value to a NEW_RV value
● Set the period value (for frequency measurement mode) to a NEW_PERIOD value
If the following Boolean flag values are set to 1 when the CTRL_HSC instruction is executed,
the corresponding NEW_xxx value is loaded to the counter. Multiple requests (more than
one flag is set at the same time) are processed in a single execution of the CTRL_HSC
instruction.

context_chunks.text:
9.2 PID control
STEP 7 provides the following PID instructions for the S7-1200 CPU:
● The PID_Compact instruction is used to control technical processes with continuous
input- and output variables.
● The PID_3Step instruction is used to control motor-actuated devices, such as valves that
require discrete signals for open- and close actuation.
Note
Changes that you make to the PID configuration and download in RUN mode do not take
effect until the CPU transitions from STOP to RUN mode.
Both PID instructions (PID_3Step and PID_Compact) can calculate the P-, I-, and D-
components during startup (if configured for "pretuning"). You can also configure the
instruction for "fine tuning" to allow you to optimize the parameters. You do not need to
manually determine the parameters.
Note
Execute the PID instruction at constant intervals of the sampling time (preferably in a cyclic
OB).
